proposals.title: Build a stable connected load path before optimizing motion
proposals.trigger: Machine construction, review, or controller revision
procedure: Translate the current public task into payload, support, clearance, connection, power and actuation constraints. Keep the official role responsibilities and tool schema.

First make one simple connected chassis with a low center of mass, symmetric support contacts and explicit attachment paths. Check every block position and orientation from tool feedback; do not assume visually close parts are connected.
Treat prescribed payload mass and geometry as fixed. Verify clearance and containment under acceleration; avoid structures whose success depends on an unverified collision or a detached support.
Use the shortest controllable mechanism that can satisfy the task. Separate movement control from payload retention and inspect torque and tipping risk before adding more actuators.
After native simulation, compare actual displacement, payload retention and stability against the requirements. Change the failed mechanism or control assumption, not unrelated decorative structure.
Complete the official construction and controller protocol. A valid build or visual plausibility is not a physics pass.
successSignals: Public construction feedback establishes connected support and usable controls
Native metrics meet every required condition
failureSignals: Actuator force or torque destabilizes the load
Controller does not match configured keys
recovery: Diagnose the first failed support, attachment or actuation constraint from public feedback and simplify the affected subsystem.
invariants: No case-specific layout, fixed seed, answer machine or pixel coordinate
Only offered tools and public feedback
